title: Last-Second Goal Stuns United!
summary:
Imagine scoring a goal so amazing that it makes the whole stadium go wild—with the very last kick of the game! That's exactly what happened to Ainsley Maitland-Niles on his debut for Everton.

The game was against Manchester United in Liverpool, England. United was winning 2-1, and it looked like they had the match in the bag. But then, in the 87th minute, Benjamin Sesko headed in a goal for United, making it 2-1. Wait, that's not right—let me start over.

Actually, here's what happened: United scored first with a great solo goal by Bryan Mbeumo early in the second half. Then Everton fought back, and Tyrique George smashed in a goal to make it 1-1. Then, with just three minutes left, Sesko headed in a cross to put United ahead 2-1. It seemed like United would win.

But then, in the very last seconds, Maitland-Niles—who had just come on as a substitute—hit a rocket from 30 yards away (that's about as long as a school bus!). The ball flew into the net, and the game ended 2-2. His teammates went crazy, and the fans roared.

Maitland-Niles said it was a dream come true to score on his debut. The draw means Everton stays unbeaten this season, with five points from three games. United has four points and is in 11th place.

Everton showed a lot of fighting spirit, even though they have a small squad. They kept trying and got their reward. It was a thrilling game that showed why soccer is so exciting—you never know what can happen until the final whistle!
why_it_matters: A game can change in the last second, so it teaches you to keep trying even when things look hard.
